blocks.heading: Rates and LCM units
lines: If a person does a job in n days, they do 1/n of it each day.
Take the LCM of the days as total work. A takes 12 days, B takes 6: use 12 units.
A does 1 a day, B does 2, together 3, so 12 ÷ 3 = 4 days.

blocks.heading: Working together
lines: Add the rates. Time = ab ÷ (a + b) for two people.
A pipe that fills and a leak that empties: subtract the rates.
Fills in 8 h, leak empties in 24 h: 1/8 − 1/24 = 1/12, so 12 h.

blocks.heading: Efficiency
lines: Efficiency is in the inverse ratio of days taken.
Wages are shared in the ratio of work done: efficiency × days worked.

blocks.heading: Men and days, alternate days
lines: Man-days = men × days is fixed. 12 men × 15 days = 180, so 9 men need 20 days.
Alternate days: find the work done in one 2-day cycle, count the cycles, then check the last day.
A 10 days, B 15 days: 1/6 per cycle, so 6 cycles, 12 days.
